_comment: Reference metadata only (schedule LENGTH, a public structural fact) — not player statistics. Used to scale qualification thresholds across eras so a fixed 100-attempt cutoff isn't applied to a 10-game 1944 season or a 9-game 1982 strike season. Bands marked 'verified' were confirmed via web search on 2026-10-28; bands marked 'approximate_unverified' come from general football-history knowledge and were NOT independently re-verified this session — treat them as a reasonable starting point to refine before relying on them for anything but scaling thresholds.

nfl_apfa_bands.notes: APFA founding season; no fixed league schedule, teams played irregular slates (roughly 6-13 games) against a mix of league and non-league opponents.
Early NFL; schedule length still varied by team (commonly 10-14 games), 12 used as an approximate midpoint.
Wartime roster shortages shortened the schedule.
Players' strike shortened the season to 9 games.
Players' strike shortened the season to 15 games.

afl_bands.notes: Pre-merger AFL; not independently re-verified this session. Kept in its own league_id ('AFL') and never pooled with NFL baselines for the same years.
